name: stanford-covid-vaccine
description: Write a Python fit_predict(train, test_inputs, time_budget_s) function that learns from 1,349 OpenVaccine RNA sequences with per-position degradation measurements and predicts reactivity, deg_Mg_pH10 and deg_Mg_50C at the first 68 positions of 240 test RNAs, within a 300 s wall-clock budget on 4 CPU threads; scored by MCRMSE (lower is better).

sources.locator: Kaggle_RYOS_trainset.csv (MIT): the SN_filter = 1 rows of the competition's train.json
Wayment-Steele et al. 2022, Deep learning models for predicting RNA degradation via dual crowdsourcing
prepare.py (240 SN_filter > 0 test rows, random_state 0) and grade.py (MCRMSE over reactivity, deg_Mg_pH10, deg_Mg_50C on scored positions)

requirements.hardware: See upstream requirements and task notes.
notes: Kaggle dataset access and competition terms

evaluation.paper_metric: mean columnwise root mean squared error

notes: Paper reports gold medal; metric and runtime depend on each competition. Configure competition ID in supplied task config.

Exact metric verified against official MLE-bench grade.py at https://github.com/openai/mle-bench/blob/507f92e1138bb6e40dac5c6ee7a6758e6424bf97/mlebench/competitions/stanford-covid-vaccine/grade.py. This dependency revision was audited; LoongFlow paper did not pin this MLE-bench revision.
Source inconsistency: config.yaml labels the grader multi-class-log-loss, but grade.py actually computes mean columnwise RMSE; this task uses the executable grading definition.
